problem: Existing multi-object search (MOS) methods either use POMDPs that scale poorly and need environment priors, DRL that generalizes poorly, or foundation-model methods (VLFM, Finder) that always go to frontiers and cannot recover from missed or occluded detections.
motivation: Open-vocabulary detectors are unreliable under occlusion and clutter, and MOS needs thorough exploration of unknown environments with several targets. A robot must therefore revisit high-value regions and replan after failures rather than abandon them once a frontier is chosen.
key_idea: Turn a VLM-derived multi-layer value map into a compact POMDP (DBSCAN candidate points plus one best frontier as actions, decayed-value belief) solved with POUCT, so the robot can trade off exploring frontiers against re-examining high-value candidate regions.
insight: The POMDP planner accounts for travel cost and the explore/exploit trade-off, which greedy selection cannot: removing it drops SR from 55.0% to 27.5% and MSPL from 0.497 to 0.154. Value decay stops the robot from fixating on misleading high-value regions: removing it drops SR to 45.0%. The qualitative comparison shows Finder abandons an occluded corner toilet, while OVAMOS revisits it and finds it.
method: Multi-layer value map: BLIP-2 cosine similarity between the RGB view and each target prompt, with a FOV cone confidence mask and confidence-weighted fusion over time; per-object maps are normalized and aggregated assuming independence
Object map and detection: Grounding DINO, YOLOv7 and SAM detect and store objects; an obstacle map and a frontier map (boundary midpoints) come from depth and odometry
Value decay: a sigmoid of per-location update count (v' = 1/(1+exp((u-tau)/kappa))) lowers the value of repeatedly observed regions where the detector finds nothing

Candidate points and belief: thresholding the decayed map and clustering with DBSCAN gives candidate points; the action space is MoveTo(candidates) plus MoveTo(best frontier); the belief is a discrete distribution over candidates proportional to value

POMDP (OO-POMDP): binary detection observation with exponential distance decay, reward = -move cost + frontier bonus + target bonus (20/500/500), gamma 0.95, solved by POUCT; in real execution the belief is updated from the decayed value map rather than by Bayes
Navigation controller: converts the chosen target location into discrete forward/left/right commands

setting.backbone: BLIP-2 (frozen, BLIP in real world) + Grounding DINO / YOLOv7 / SAM + POUCT planner
setting.action_space: MoveTo high-level goals (candidate points / frontier) executed as discrete low-level forward/turn left/turn right
setting.privileged: none (ground-truth shortest path used only for the MSPL metric)

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 HM3D validation scenes, 120 self-constructed episodes, each with 3 target objects, max 500 steps, success radius 1 m

numbers_note: Only a self-built 5-scene, 120-episode HM3D MOS benchmark is reported; the real-world test is qualitative only (6'56" for 3 objects).
results: On 120 three-object HM3D episodes, OVAMOS reaches 55.0% SR and 0.497 MSPL, versus Finder (28.3%, 0.198), VLFM (12.5%, 0.075) and Random Walk (0%). A real TurtleBot recovered an occluded umbrella in a 50 m² office.
limitations: Restricted to 2D maps, a simple action space and a fixed camera viewpoint
Small self-built evaluation (5 scenes, 120 episodes), with no standard benchmark and only a qualitative real-robot test with a smaller VLM (BLIP)
Independence assumption across objects; many hand-tuned parameters
